Title: Machine learning based multi- stage intrusion detection system and feature selection ensemble security in cloud assisted vehicular ad hoc networks
Text:
Machine learning based multi-
stage intrusion detection system 
and feature selection ensemble 
security in cloud assisted vehicular 
ad hoc networks
C. Christy1, A. Nirmala2, A. Mary Odilya Teena2 & A. Isabella Amali2
The development of intelligent transportation systems relies heavily on Cloud-assisted Vehicular 
Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs); hence, these networks must be protected. Particularly susceptible to 
a broad range of assaults are VANETs because of their extreme dynamism and decentralization. 
Connected vehicles’ safety and efficiency could be compromised if these security threats materialize, 
leading to disastrous road accidents. Solving these issues will require an advanced Intrusion Detection 
System (IDS) with real-time threat recognition and neutralization capabilities. A new method for 
improving VANET security, a multi-stage Lightweight IntrusionDetection System Using Random 
Forest Algorithms (MLIDS-RFA), focuses on feature selection and ensemble models based on 
machine learning (ML). A multi-step approach is employed by the proposed system, with each stage 
dedicated to accurately detecting specific types of attacks. Regarding feature selection, MLIDS-RFA 
uses machine-learning approaches to enhance the detection process. The outcome is a reduction in 
the amount of processing overhead and a shortening of the response times. The detection abilities 
of ensemble models are enhanced by integrating the strengths of the Random Forest algorithm 
(RFA), which safeguards against intricate dangers. The practicality of the proposed technology is 
demonstrated by conducting thorough simulation analyses. This research demonstrates that the 
system can reduce false positives while maintaining high detection rates. This research ensures next-
generation transport networks’ secure and reliable functioning and prepares the path for VANET 
protection upgrades. MLIDS-RFA has improved detection accuracy (96.2%) and computing efficiency 
(94.8%) for dynamic VANET management. It operates well with large networks (97.8%) and adapts well 
to network changes (93.8%). The comprehensive methodology ensures high detection performance 
(95.9%) and VANET security by balancing accuracy, efficiency, and scalability.
Keywords  Intrusion-detection, Machine learning, Security, Vehicular ad hoc network, Lightweight
Intrusion detection in VANETs is typically based primarily on anomaly-based methods, and detecting danger 
is their goal1. Based on signature approaches in dynamic systems like VANETs, where new attack vectors are 
constantly developed, they struggle to detect new ones using a database of known attack patterns2. Because 
of this, they are less effective than others; however, anomaly-based detection systems attempt to identify 
deviations from patterns3. Due to their inability to scale or adapt, traditional systems are slow to detect and 
respond to threats, while VANETs are mobile and decentralized4. Additional bandwidth and processing power 
are needed for these methods, devices with limited VANET resources have a problem, lack of feature selection-
ensemble model synergy made previous approaches less accurate and more vulnerable to complex attacks, 
VANETs’ complex and multi-dimensional threats make single-layer security solutions ineffective5. Therefore, 
conventional methods often fail to provide strong, real-time intrusion detection for VANET security; more 
advanced detection methods using ML and ensemble modeling are emphasized6.

Creating and deploying multi-stage IDS for VANETs using ensemble models and ML-based feature selection 
is complex and multifaceted7. One of the main challenges in VANETs is keeping up with all the moving elements 
because vehicles constantly change their network connections8. Due to mobility, data streams and network 
topologies change often, making detection accuracy and real-time analysis difficult9. VANET data’s high 
dimensionality makes feature selection harder, and data includes communication protocols, sensor readings, 
and GPS. Because the model may grow overloaded with unnecessary features, calculations may slow down 
and become less efficient10. An effective ensemble model of neural networks, decision trees, and support vector 
machines must be balanced to avoid overestimation or underfitting, which can impair detection accuracy11. 
Processing in real-time with low latency is another obstacle, and risk detection delays can cause accidents and 
traffic obstructions12. VANETs are vulnerable to spoofing and DDoS attacks; therefore, the IDS must adapt, 
although it is common to train and update ML models in such a dynamic context, which may strain network 
resources. These powerful IDS systems are challenging to deploy while safeguarding data privacy and vehicle 
communication since an intrusion could compromise the entire security system13.
A multi-stage IDS with ML feature selection is described in this research to construct a vehicle network safety 
strategy14. This architecture optimizes network component identification by decreasing computing overhead15. 
Ensemble models enhance accuracy and resistance to attacks by utilizing several classifiers. Due to its ability to 
increase detection rates and respond instantly to emerging threats, this technology greatly simplifies protecting 
vehicle communication networks16.
Smart transport systems rely on VANETs, which are dynamic, decentralized networks; however, these 
networks aren’t immune to security flaws that compromise vehicle efficiency and safety and could lead to 
catastrophic accidents17. Implementing an advanced IDS to identify and address real-time threats is the simplest 
option. Complex network systems challenge rapid processing and precise threat detection18. Strengthening 
VANET security is possible using an IDS that uses an ensemble model and selects features based on ML.
Cloud computing is essential to the suggested study framework because it allows for the efficient, scalable, 
and real-time processing of intrusion detection activities. Centralized model training, large-scale traffic analysis, 
and high-performance data storage are the main uses of the cloud architecture. Devices near the network’s 
periphery or in moving vehicles have less latency and fewer resource limitations thanks to the system’s ability to 
transfer computationally heavy tasks to the cloud. The cloud makes it easy to update models and deploy them 
to different nodes at once, so it is always protected against new threats. In addition, the model’s capacity to 
identify intricate multi-vector assaults is improved by integrating cloud services, which enable the aggregation 
of varied data streams from many sources (such as the Internet of Vehicles, CPS, and vehicular networks). This 
centralized design allows for dynamic scalability according to traffic demand and provides parallel training with 
GPU-accelerated resources. In resource-constrained vehicle environments, the cloud improves the suggested 
IDS accuracy, dependability, and flexibility while keeping costs low and energy efficient.
Vehicle networks are vulnerable to a variety of advanced cyber threats, such as zero-day and multi-vector 
attacks, due to the fast development of Cloud-assisted Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (C-VANETs), the ever-
increasing amount of heterogeneous data and the open, decentralized communication environment. Regarding 
latency-sensitive and resource-constrained VANET settings, traditional IDS aren’t always up to snuff regarding 
real-time threat identification. This is because of their high computing costs, huge model sizes, and restricted 
scalability. Lightweight, scalable, multi-stage intelligent detection systems that can guarantee high detection 
accuracy with low computing costs are needed to address this increasing risk. In response to these difficulties, 
the authors of this study present MLIDS-RFA, a multi-stage Lightweight IDS that improves detection efficiency, 
decreases false positives, and guarantees adaptability in scenarios involving dynamically changing vehicular 
networks by utilizing ensemble learning and feature selection.
The main contribution of the paper is.
•	 Developing a multi-tiered IDS that utilizes ML to detect and classify the assaults that can impact VANETs 
efficiently.
•	 Employing Random Forest and feature selection techniques to decrease processing overhead and reaction 
times, ensuring effective real-time threat analysis.
•	 A more secure and reliable VANET can be achieved by using ensemble models to improve detection rates and 
decrease the amount of false positives.
The literature review findings are in Section II, an experiment entitled multi-stage IDS Utilising ML-Based 
Feature Selection and Ensemble Models for Enhanced Security in Cloud-assisted Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks, 
which builds on these findings. Section III describes mathematically on MLIDS-RFA. After the findings, the 
implications are discussed in section IV. Section V contains a summary and concluding suggestions.
Literature survey
IDS is crucial in safeguarding contemporary networks from cyberattacks, especially as technology advances 
in automotive Ethernet, the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), and other networked devices. Consequently, IDS has 
become more crucial.
A Random Forest and a Pruned Convolutional Neural Network (RF & PCNN) are combined in the proposed 
approach for IDS by da Luz, L. F. M. et al.19. This method achieves rapid detection with comparable rates and a 
reduction in the number of false positives in automotive Ethernet networks.
When it comes to balanced, efficient, and precise multi-class intrusion detection in IoV, the proposed method 
by Gou W et al.20 makes use of an adaptive tree-based ensemble network (AT-EN) with SMOTE and Random 
Under Sampler; this method achieves high F1-scores.

Amouri A. et al.21 suggested an IDS that uses cross-layer detection (C-LD) in conjunction with heuristic 
AMoF and linear regression. This system can obtain detection rates of over 98% for high power/velocity scenarios 
and over 90% for environments with lower conditions.
Yang, L22. proposed a multi-tiered hybrid HIDS. This system combines signature-based and anomaly-based 
detection, and it achieves an accuracy rate of 99.99% and 99.88% on known assaults, as well as strong F1 scores 
for zero-day attacks, all while requiring little processing time.
An approach to anomaly detection in IDS (AD-IDS) has been proposed by Azam Z et al.23 using a decision 
tree. With this simple and fast procedure, people can learn how to decrease the number of false positives in 
network security and increase the accuracy of the detections.
Saheed and Chukwuere24 suggested the eXplainable AI ensemble transfer learning for zero-day botnet 
attack recognition in the IoV (XAIEnsembleTL-IoV). By using deep Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), 
the suggested model makes judgments more transparent and easier for cybersecurity experts to grasp. To 
further improve computational efficiency, the model uses BiLAE, which stands for hybrid bidirectional LSTM 
and autoencoders, to decrease the dimensionality of traffic in IoV networks. In binary-class scenarios for 
interior vehicular (CAN) networks, the model attained 100% precision, accuracy, F1-score, recall, and Matthew 
Correlation Coefficients. In multi-class scenarios for exterior vehicular networks (N-BaIoT), the model attained 
99% accuracy and similarly high metrics. With less dependence on massive datasets, the model outperformed 
existing approaches in identifying zero-day botnet assaults.
Yakub Kayode Saheed and Sanjay Misra25 proposed the explainable privacy-preserving DNN for resilient 
anomaly recognition in Cyber-Physical Systems-empowered IoT networks (CPS-IoT-PPDNN). To help users 
and cybersecurity specialists validate and strengthen the system’s resilience, this framework uses a Shpley additive 
explanations (SHAP) approach to elucidate the decision-making procedure of the DNN. The method yielded 
remarkable outcomes when evaluated on the cutting-edge X-IIoTID and Edge-IIoTset datasets. Both datasets 
hit 100% accuracy, recall, precision, and F1-score for binary classification. In multi-class situations, Edge-IIoTset 
obtained 99.98% accuracy and X-IIoTID 99.99%. On top of that, our model demonstrated far quicker training 
times while maintaining testing efficiency. Enhancing the defenses of CPS-IoT networks against modern cyber 
threats, the findings demonstrate that the suggested explainable DNN architecture delivers powerful intrusion 
identification in real-time while safeguarding privacy.
Yakub Kayode Saheed et al.26 recommended lightweight threat detection in the industrial IoT via a genetic 
algorithm with an attention mechanism and LSTM on multivariate time series sensor data (GA-mADAM-
IIoT). The six components that make up the GA-mADAM-IIoT are the following: attention module (AM), 
communication module (CM), intrusion detection, activity receiver, mitigation, and alarm. The GA was 
developed with dimensionality and an assortment of features, and it was trained using data from network flows 
via an LSTM network. Comparing the suggested model against state-of-the-art models revealed impressive 
results: a recall of 99.98%, precision of 99.98%, F1 of 99.98%, and MCC of 99.66% on SWaT data, in addition to 
an excellent accuracy of 99.98% and AUC of 100%.
Zhiquan Liu et al.27 presented the Privacy-Preserving Reputation Updating (PPRU) for Cloud-Assisted 
Vehicular Networks using Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) and Paillier algorithms. The trustworthy 
but inquisitive cloud provider (CSP) gathers and preprocesses reputation feedback to protect user privacy, 
substantially reducing compute overheads by 88.36% and communication overheads by 83.88% on the TA side, 
respectively. The suggested method, meanwhile, may provide powerful reputation management, security, and 
privacy preservation with reasonable communication and computation overheads. The extensive theoretical 
study and simulation assessment findings show that the suggested system is far better than the current schemes 
in several respects.
Zhiquan Liu et al.28 introduced Privacy-Preserving Trust Management (PPTM) for Emergency Message 
Distribution in Space–Air–Ground-Integrated Vehicular Networks (SAGIVNs). In addition to its appealing 
qualities, such as broad applicability and robustness, the suggested approach can provide accurate trust 
management and strong conditional privacy preservation concurrently with a small communication cost. A 
complete theoretical analysis and simulation assessment are provided. The findings show that compared to the 
current systems, the suggested one is better in several ways.
Jingjing Guo et al.29 examined the Reinforcement Learning-based Context-Awareness Trust Model (TROVE) 
for VANETs. In the proposed system, the evaluation approach and associated information are used to calculate the 
trust assessment result of an evaluation request. This evaluation result is independent of the trust level of entities 
in the network and the existence of contradictory evidence. In addition, the author develops a reinforcement 
learning model that enables cars to modify their assessment approach to keep an accurate assessment outcome 
across various driving situations. The author ran extensive tests to ensure the suggested model worked under 
various driving situations. Regardless of the fraction of malicious nodes in the network, our model can adapt to 
diverse driving circumstances with low time overhead.

Several limitations have not been addressed, even if the research that was examined shows that IDS for 
automotive networks has come a long way. Current approaches often make concessions in detection accuracy, 
computational efficiency, and real-time responsiveness. These include adaptive ensemble techniques, cross-layer 
detection mechanisms, and hybrid CNN-RF models. When it comes to dynamic VANET settings, many methods 
aren’t scalable, have high processing costs, or operate poorly in the face of unbalanced traffic or zero-day assaults. 
Additionally, most current solutions aren’t deployable on resource-constrained vehicular edge nodes since they 
don’t optimize feature selection and have lightweight design. These constraints highlight the necessity for a 
multi-stage, lightweight intrusion detection framework like the proposed MLIDS-RFA. This framework achieves 
a balance between high detection accuracy, low false positive rates, minimal latency, and low computational cost,

Proposed method
Intelligent transportation systems rely on Cloud-assisted Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) to improve 
road safety and efficiency via communication between cars and infrastructure. Several security risks, including 
counterfeiting, denial of service (DoS), and data modification attacks, may affect VANETs due to their dynamic 
and decentralized nature. The data integrity and the safety of vehicles are set to the vulnerabilities based on a 
series of threats required for robust security. Using ensemble models and feature selection based on ML, this 
work presents MLIDS-RFA, which uses the Random Forest Algorithm to mitigate various security vulnerabilities 
in VANETs successfully.
Building an intruder detection system with multiple levels of protection
A new (MLIDS-RFA) developed for use in Cloud assisted Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) is introduced 
in this research. The assaults in the network are set to different steps, detecting the phase run designed by the 
system. This improves the detection efficacy and makes the system more resilient against various security threats.

Combining feature selection based on ML
Regarding VANET intrusion detection, the suggested solution uses a feature selection process based on ML 
to find the best features. Due to this focused method, processing overhead and reaction time are drastically 
reduced, allowing for continuous monitoring and mitigation of risks in dynamic vehicle contexts, as shown in 
Fig. 2.
In the extraction of features, multi-dimensional characteristics are mapped to a lower-dimensional space for 
features to reduce the amount of data properties. You may think of this transformation as a hybrid of linear and 
non-linear features, and it keeps all the important parts of the original features. The resulting feature space displays 
characteristics that are comparable to the initial features. Methods for extracting pertinent characteristics from 
a dataset are known as feature selection methods. Improving the efficiency and effectiveness of learning models’ 
computations relies heavily on feature extraction and selecting features. As a result, both strategies might be seen 
as successful ways to feature engineering. Extracting features that may enhance the effectiveness of the learning 
system is where feature extraction shines. It is important to remember that the feature extractor changes the 
features’ meaning, which might make further analysis more difficult. The selection of features maintains the 
features’ initial physical significance, as opposed to feature extraction. To do this, it takes the whole collection 
of characteristics and selects just the most important ones. Since they can potentially improve learning models’ 
efficiency and comprehension, the selection of features and extraction take center stage in feature engineering.

The (MLIDS-RFA) is presented in this paper. The technology is intended to recognize particular network 
threats in many phases. The comprehensive protection of VANETs is ensured by this multi-stage technique, 
which increases detection accuracy and resistance against diverse security threats.
A Multi-Layer Vehicle VIDS is shown in Fig. 3 as an example of its design. This technology will make vehicular 
networks more secure and dependable by identifying and countering possible dangers. The architectural 
Collection of Data Layer collects information from various vehicle data sources and communication methods. 
This layer guarantees the thorough collection of data from the vehicle’s surroundings. The next step is to refine 
the data using the preprocessing layer. Data cleansing involves removing errors and outliers, extracting features 
to find important qualities, and selecting characteristics to rank the distinctive characteristics for additional 
investigation. The data quality creates a vital layer with the work based on the detection method.
The method variety is used by possible intrusion with irregularities based on the spots by the detection 
layer at various stages of a system relying on foundations. To enhance detection accuracy while decreasing 
false positives, it employs the detection of anomaly methods, signature approaches, behavioral modeling, and 
a comprehensive decision mechanism. The Response Layer kicks in when it senses an incursion. Notifications, 
intrusion mitigation measures, and reporting log maintenance are all under the purview of this layer. Timely 
and suitable reactions are guaranteed in response to threats that are discovered. The Feedback & Learning Layer 
allows the system to improve using learning and feedback loops continuously. This layer enables the system to 
adjust to new threats by incorporating fresh data and learning from past reactions.
An effective IDS may be built using ML and predictive modeling techniques. Training supervised learning 
algorithms on tagged data, where intrusions are categorized as either benign or malicious, allows for real-time 
intrusion detection and categorization. As shown in the highlighted part of Fig. 4, our study enhanced the 
architecture by strategically positioning the IDS to filter all critical communications, human interactions, and 
environmental interactions for intrusion. Clustering is a kind of unsupervised learning that may be used to 
spot out-of-the-ordinary patterns and uncover previously unknown dangers. Regarding autonomous vehicle 
intrusion detection, evaluating many machine-learning models and looking at their performance measures 
like F1-score, recall, accuracy, and precision is important. Below, you can find the specifics of these steps. It is 
common practice to handle raw data before preparing it for use in a machine-learning model. This is the first 
and most important stage in developing a machine-learning model. The data preparation process in this study 
included cleaning all three datasets. Data cleaning included filtering out unwanted noise. At this point, the study 
dealt with missing data by deleting or replacing them with an average value. To make the data usable, all outliers 
and useless characteristics were removed. At this stage, this study normalized the data by, if needed, scaling the 
characteristics to a common range. Data normalization involves scaling the values of attributes in a dataset as a 
data preparation technique. The process of standardization entails adjusting the data so that it follows a normal 
distribution. A standard normal distribution is a distribution where the mean is zero and the standard deviation 
is one.

The MLIDS-RFA improves detection accuracy by using ensemble models, namely the Random Forest Algorithm 
(RFA), to harness the capabilities of several weak classifiers. The attack patterns are complicated by ensemble 
methods and identifying false positive aspects with the security level.
The network defenses are strengthened by the data mining-based features depending on the choice and 
ensemble models where the image showcases the VANET IDS. The first step of the system’s Data Collection Stage

is used to detect any network security risks. In the Feature Identification Stage, the system analyzes the acquired 
data using the Random Forest Algorithm (RFA) to identify the most relevant characteristics. Through a laser-like

With its multi-stage IDS, the proposed MLIDS-RFA can identify and counter various threats, making VANETs 
more secure. First, the approach uses a feature selection technique based on ML to find the most important 
information for intrusion detection, which speeds up reaction times and reduces processing overhead. The 
system then uses an ensemble model technique, namely the Random Forest Algorithm, to combine numerous 
weak classifiers and enhance detection accuracy. Using this route, the detection system may successfully identify 
intricate attack patterns with few false positives and good detection rates. Simulated results show that the system 
can secure VANETs, which is crucial for the future generation of transportation networks to have secure and 
dependable communication.
To improve detection accuracy, the MLIDS-RFA combines several weak classifiers using ensemble models, 
particularly the Random Forest Algorithm. This method enhances the system’s capacity to detect intricate 
patterns of attacks in VANETs. Consequently, it improves the network’s security in general and decreases the 
number of false positives.
Results and discussion
A multi-stage IDS performance in VANETs is assessed in the present investigation, and the MLIDS-RFA IDS 
uses ML-based feature selection and ensemble models. It evaluates detection accuracy, computing efficiency, 
scalability, network adaption, and discovery performance. A benchmark dataset created to aid in developing and 
assessing intrusion detection systems under realistic network settings, the CICIDS2017 dataset30 stands for the 
Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity Intrusion Detection System 2017. Using a testbed that closely resembles 
real-world business network settings, it includes a full mix of malicious and benign network traffic. Including 
one benign class and 15 other attack methods, such as DoS, DDoS, brute force, web-based assaults, infiltration, 
botnet, and Heartbleed, the dataset covers 16 categories and represents modern cybersecurity threats. Tools like 
CICFlowMeter gather over 80 statistical and behavioral aspects from each traffic flow, including the flow length, 
the packet size, the information in the header, and the inter-arrival time. There is a noticeable class imbalance in 
the CICIDS2017 dataset, with certain attack categories being much overrepresented. Despite this, the dataset is 
still a great resource for supervised and unsupervised learning methods in network security. More so for minority 
groups, this mismatch might cause prejudiced learning and poor generalization. For cyber-physical systems 
(CPS), the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), and vehicular networks (VANETs), where adaptive detection mechanisms 
are crucial, CICIDS2017 is a great place to test intelligent intrusion detection models for scalability, accuracy, 
and robustness. To improve the model’s dependability and fairness across all attack categories, researchers often 
use balancing procedures like SMOTE, cost-sensitive learning, or ensemble approaches to reduce the skewed 
distribution.
The fundamental classifier in this system is the Random Forest Algorithm (RFA), which has been fine-tuned 
with the following hyperparameters: 150 estimators, 30 as the maximum depth, 2 as the minimum sample per 
leaf, 4 as the minimum sample to split, Gini impurity as the splitting criterion, and ‘sqrt’ as the maximum 
number of features considered at each split. Feature selection utilizes Mutual Information Gain and Recursive 
Feature Elimination (RFE) to minimize computing burden and complexity while keeping essential qualities.
Key performance indicators such as latency, model size, memory footprint, and computational cost were used 
to evaluate the MLIDS-RFA model in the context of VANETs, where real-time decision-making and resource 
efficiency are crucial. The goal was to determine if the model could be practically deployed in this setting.

To achieve a more equitable distribution of classes, synthetic minority class samples are generated using the 
Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE). This method improves the Random Forest classifier’s 
capacity to identify uncommon but crucial assault patterns while reducing its bias toward majority classes. With 
SMOTE, Random Under Sampling (RUS) is used to avoid overfitting when data is oversampled. Stratified K-fold 
cross-validation follows the hybrid resampling process to maintain class proportions during model assessment 
further. Improved recall and F1 scores for minority intrusion classes, reduced false negatives, and a model 
sensitive to uncommon intrusions rather than too accurate result from this balancing strategy’s success.
Conclusion and future works
The MLIDS-RFA greatly improves vehicle ad hoc network security, resolving VANETs’ core decentralized 
and dynamic architecture concerns. The system uses a multi-stage strategy to identify and eliminate threats, 
speeding response times and improving detection. ML-based feature selection accelerates and improves threat 
detection by lowering processing overhead. Ensemble models, particularly Random Forest algorithms, defend 
against complex and changing threats. This safeguard may lower false positives without hurting detection, and
